name: UML
description: UML 2.5.1 structure and behaviour diagrams: class, component, package, deployment, use case, activity and state machine, with typed member rows, the relationship ends of the standard, its constraints as rules and starting templates.

glyphs.label: Note
glyphs.source: drawn from UML 2.5.1 (OMG formal/17-12-05), 7.2.4 Comment notation: a rectangle with its upper right corner bent

elementTypes.label: Note
elementTypes.description: A comment attached to elements with note anchors.

relationshipTypes.label: Association
relationshipTypes.description: A structural link between classifiers, with a role and multiplicity at each end.

relationshipTypes.label: Composition
relationshipTypes.description: A whole that owns its parts: the source is the whole, the target the part.

relationshipTypes.label: Aggregation
relationshipTypes.description: A shared whole and part: the source is the whole, the target the part.

relationshipTypes.label: Generalization
relationshipTypes.description: The source specializes the target (the child points at the parent).

relationshipTypes.label: Realization
relationshipTypes.description: The source implements the contract of the target interface.

relationshipTypes.label: Dependency
relationshipTypes.description: The source needs the target to be complete.

relationshipTypes.label: Usage
relationshipTypes.description: The source uses the target to work.

relationshipTypes.label: Note Anchor
relationshipTypes.description: Attaches a note to an element.

rules.description: UML allows this relationship only between certain kinds of element.
rules.reference: UML 2.5.1, 9.9.17 InterfaceRealization (a realization targets an interface) and the relationship tables of clauses 7 to 19

rules.description: A part belongs to at most one whole at a time.
rules.reference: UML 2.5.1, 9.5.3 composite aggregation: a part is included in at most one composite object at a time

rules.description: A classifier cannot be its own ancestor.
A multiplicity is written n, *, n..m or n..* with n at most m.
rules.reference: UML 2.5.1, 7.5.4 MultiplicityElement notation and 7.8.8.8 constraint upper_ge_lower

rules.description: Attribute names in one classifier must be distinct.
The association's ends should show its navigability.
rules.reference: UML 2.5.1, 11.5.4 Association notation: an open arrowhead marks a navigable end

rules.description: UML property values must fit their types.
This kind of UML element does not belong on this kind of diagram.
Every UML connector should join two elements.

rulesets.label: UML 2.5.1
rulesets.description: The well-formedness constraints of UML 2.5.1 (OMG formal/17-12-05) that a drawing can show, plus house rules for consistent diagrams.

variants.label: Visibility in words
variants.description: Member rows spell visibility out (public, private) instead of using symbols.

variants.label: Lollipop interfaces
variants.description: Interfaces drawn as balls on plain realization lines.

variants.label: Names only
variants.description: Classifiers show their names with the member compartments left empty.

elementTypes.label: Class
elementTypes.description: A classifier with attributes and operations.

properties.label: Attributes
properties.description: One attribute per line: visibility name: Type [multiplicity] = default.

properties.label: Operations
properties.description: One operation per line: visibility name(parameters): Return.

properties.label: Stereotype
properties.description: Shown as a keyword above the name; empty for none.

elementTypes.label: Interface
elementTypes.description: A contract of operations that classes and components realize.

properties.label: Attributes
properties.description: One attribute per line: visibility name: Type [multiplicity] = default.

properties.label: Operations
properties.description: One operation per line: visibility name(parameters): Return.

properties.label: Stereotype
properties.description: Shown as a keyword above the name; empty for none.

elementTypes.label: Enumeration
elementTypes.description: A data type whose values are listed literals.

viewpoints.label: Class Diagram
viewpoints.description: Classes, interfaces and enumerations with their relationships.

rules.description: An interface no classifier realizes is not yet provided by anything.
rules.reference: UML 2.5.1, 10.4.4 Interface notation (provided interfaces); an approximation

templates.label: Class Diagram
templates.description: A small order model: classes with typed attributes and operations, an interface and its realization, composition and multiplicities.

glyphs.label: Component
glyphs.source: drawn from UML 2.5.1 (OMG formal/17-12-05), 11.6.4 Component notation: a classifier rectangle with the component icon in its upper right corner

elementTypes.label: Component
elementTypes.description: A replaceable part of a system that provides and requires interfaces.

viewpoints.label: Component Diagram
viewpoints.description: Components with the interfaces they provide and require.

templates.label: Component Diagram
templates.description: Three components wired through the interfaces they provide and use.

glyphs.label: Package
glyphs.source: drawn from UML 2.5.1 (OMG formal/17-12-05), 12.2.4 Package notation: a large rectangle with a small rectangle (a tab) attached to its upper left

elementTypes.label: Package
elementTypes.description: A namespace that groups packageable elements.

relationshipTypes.label: Package Import
relationshipTypes.description: The source namespace imports the public names of the target package.

relationshipTypes.label: Package Merge
relationshipTypes.description: The source package is extended by the contents of the target package.

viewpoints.label: Package Diagram
viewpoints.description: Packages and the imports, merges and dependencies between them.

rules.description: Packages should not import each other in a circle.
rules.reference: UML 2.5.1, 12.2.3 PackageImport semantics; a house rule against circular layering

templates.label: Package Diagram
templates.description: A layered application: user interface, domain and persistence packages with their imports.

glyphs.label: Node
glyphs.source: drawn from UML 2.5.1 (OMG formal/17-12-05), 19.5.4 Node notation: a perspective view of a cube

glyphs.label: Device
glyphs.source: drawn from UML 2.5.1 (OMG formal/17-12-05), 19.5.4 Node notation (Device is a Node with the keyword device)

glyphs.label: Execution Environment
glyphs.source: drawn from UML 2.5.1 (OMG formal/17-12-05), 19.5.4 Node notation (ExecutionEnvironment is a Node with the keyword executionEnvironment)

glyphs.label: Artifact
glyphs.source: drawn from UML 2.5.1 (OMG formal/17-12-05), 19.3.4 Artifact notation: a classifier rectangle with the keyword artifact and a document icon in the corner

elementTypes.label: Node
elementTypes.description: A computational resource artifacts are deployed on.

elementTypes.label: Device
elementTypes.description: A physical computational resource.

elementTypes.label: Execution Environment
elementTypes.description: A software platform inside a node that runs deployed artifacts.

elementTypes.label: Artifact
elementTypes.description: A physical piece of information such as a file or a binary.

relationshipTypes.label: Deployment
relationshipTypes.description: The source artifact is deployed on the target node.

relationshipTypes.label: Manifestation
relationshipTypes.description: The source artifact embodies the target element.

relationshipTypes.label: Communication Path
relationshipTypes.description: Nodes that exchange signals and messages.

viewpoints.label: Deployment Diagram
viewpoints.description: Nodes and the artifacts deployed on them.

rules.description: An artifact with no deployment is not placed on any node (nesting it in a node shows the same).

templates.label: Deployment Diagram
templates.description: A web server and a database server with the artifacts deployed on them.

glyphs.label: Actor
glyphs.source: drawn from UML 2.5.1 (OMG formal/17-12-05), 18.2.4 Actor notation: a stick man figure

elementTypes.label: Actor
elementTypes.description: A role a user or another system plays toward the subject.

elementTypes.label: Use Case
elementTypes.description: A behaviour the subject offers its actors.

elementTypes.label: Subject
elementTypes.description: The system whose use cases are shown: the boundary rectangle.

relationshipTypes.label: Include
relationshipTypes.description: The base use case always includes the target use case.

relationshipTypes.label: Extend
relationshipTypes.description: The source use case may extend the target use case.

viewpoints.label: Use Case Diagram
viewpoints.description: Actors, the use cases they take part in and the subject's boundary.

rules.description: Every use case should serve an actor, directly or through other use cases.
rules.reference: UML 2.5.1, 18.1.3 Use cases semantics: a use case is performed for its actors

templates.label: Use Case Diagram
templates.description: A customer and a clerk with the use cases of an online shop.

glyphs.label: Activity Final
glyphs.source: drawn from UML 2.5.1 (OMG formal/17-12-05), 15.3.4 ActivityFinalNode notation: a solid circle with a hollow circle around it

glyphs.label: Flow Final
glyphs.source: drawn from UML 2.5.1 (OMG formal/17-12-05), 15.3.4 FlowFinalNode notation: a circle with an X inside

glyphs.label: Send Signal
glyphs.source: drawn from UML 2.5.1 (OMG formal/17-12-05), 16.3.4 SendSignalAction notation: a convex pentagon

glyphs.label: Accept Event
glyphs.source: drawn from UML 2.5.1 (OMG formal/17-12-05), 16.10.4 AcceptEventAction notation: a concave pentagon

glyphs.label: Time Event
glyphs.source: drawn from UML 2.5.1 (OMG formal/17-12-05), 16.10.4 AcceptEventAction notation for a time event: an hourglass

elementTypes.label: Initial Node
elementTypes.description: Where control enters the activity.

elementTypes.label: Activity Final
elementTypes.description: Ends the whole activity.

elementTypes.label: Flow Final
elementTypes.description: Ends one flow, leaving the others running.

elementTypes.label: Action
elementTypes.description: One step of the activity.

elementTypes.label: Object Node
elementTypes.description: An object flowing between actions.

elementTypes.label: Decision
elementTypes.description: Chooses one outgoing flow by its guard; also merges flows.

elementTypes.label: Fork
elementTypes.description: Splits one flow into concurrent flows.

elementTypes.label: Join
elementTypes.description: Waits for concurrent flows and joins them.

elementTypes.label: Partition
elementTypes.description: A swimlane grouping the actions one participant performs.

elementTypes.label: Send Signal
elementTypes.description: Sends a signal.

elementTypes.label: Accept Event
elementTypes.description: Waits for an event.

elementTypes.label: Time Event
elementTypes.description: Waits for a time.

relationshipTypes.label: Control Flow
relationshipTypes.description: Control passes from the source node to the target node.

viewpoints.label: Activity Diagram
viewpoints.description: Actions, the control flow between them and the nodes that route it.

rules.description: Every action should be reachable from an initial node.
rules.reference: UML 2.5.1, 15.2.3 Activity semantics: tokens start at initial nodes

rules.description: A join synchronizes two or more flows.

templates.label: Activity Diagram
templates.description: An order handled from receipt to shipping, with packing and billing in parallel.

glyphs.label: Final State
glyphs.source: drawn from UML 2.5.1 (OMG formal/17-12-05), 14.2.4 FinalState notation: a circle surrounding a small solid filled circle

glyphs.label: Shallow History
glyphs.source: drawn from UML 2.5.1 (OMG formal/17-12-05), 14.2.4 Pseudostate notation: shallow history is a small circle containing H

glyphs.label: Deep History
glyphs.source: drawn from UML 2.5.1 (OMG formal/17-12-05), 14.2.4 Pseudostate notation: deep history is a small circle containing H*

glyphs.label: Terminate
glyphs.source: drawn from UML 2.5.1 (OMG formal/17-12-05), 14.2.4 Pseudostate notation: terminate is a cross

elementTypes.label: State Machine
elementTypes.description: The behaviour that holds the regions, states and transitions.

elementTypes.label: Region
elementTypes.description: A concurrent part of a state machine or composite state.

elementTypes.label: State
elementTypes.description: A situation the object stays in while it waits or does something.

elementTypes.label: Initial
elementTypes.description: The default entry of a region.

elementTypes.label: Final State
elementTypes.description: The region is complete.

elementTypes.label: Choice
elementTypes.description: A dynamic branch: guards are evaluated when it is reached.

elementTypes.label: Junction
elementTypes.description: A static branch or merge of transitions.

elementTypes.label: Fork
elementTypes.description: Splits a transition into concurrent regions.

elementTypes.label: Join
elementTypes.description: Merges transitions from concurrent regions.

elementTypes.label: Shallow History
elementTypes.description: Resumes the most recent direct substate.

elementTypes.label: Deep History
elementTypes.description: Resumes the most recent nested configuration.

elementTypes.label: Terminate
elementTypes.description: Ends the state machine's object.

relationshipTypes.label: Transition
relationshipTypes.description: The object moves from the source state to the target state.

viewpoints.label: State Machine Diagram
viewpoints.description: States, pseudostates and the transitions between them.

rules.description: A region has at most one initial pseudostate.
Every state should be reachable from an initial pseudostate.
rules.reference: UML 2.5.1, 14.2.3 State machine semantics: a region is entered at its initial pseudostate

rules.description: A state with no way out can never be left.
rules.reference: House rule; a composite state left by its final state is an exception

rules.description: A choice needs at least two outgoing transitions.
A join merges two or more transitions.

templates.label: State Machine Diagram
templates.description: The life of an order from pending to shipped or cancelled.
